title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the Applied ML team’s standards and operational procedures for onboarding models into the eval-harness, creating and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, defining quality guardrails, authoring quantization profiles, and executing regression triage. The goal is to ensure consistent model quality, measurable evaluation, and deterministic regression response for production inference on Redwood’s platform.

Scope

- Eval harness onboarding for new model artifacts (open weights, fine-tuned variants, quantized builds)
- Prompt set creation, labeling, and benchmark publication
- Quality guardrails definition and monitoring (acceptance criteria and alert thresholds)
- Quantization profile authoring and validation workflow
- Regression triage playbook and escalation path

Owner and contacts

- Playbook owner: Applied ML (model-quality) squad
- Primary contact: Priya Shah (Applied ML) — priya@redwood.ai
- Secondary contacts: Liam O'Connor (Eval Infrastructure), Mei Chen (Serving Runtime)

Key definitions

- Eval-harness: The CI-driven evaluation system that runs prompt sets, metrics, and produces regression/diff reports for model artifacts.
- Prompt set: Curated input set + reference outputs + metadata used to evaluate a capability or feature.
- Guardrail: Thresholds on metric or behavioral checks (toxicity, hallucination, accuracy, latency) that block promotion to hosted traffic.
- Quantization profile: A description of quantization knobs (bits, per-channel/per-tensor, symmetric/asymmetric, runtime flags) and test vectors used to validate accuracy + perf.

Onboarding checklist (new model artifact)

1. Pre-onboarding review (owner: model-owner)
   1. Confirm license & compliance (OSS license scan, provenance).
   2. Provide model card draft: architecture, tokenizer, training corpus summary, intended use.
   3. Define target workloads (chat, instruction, embeddings, reranking) and expected SLOs.

2. Artifact packaging (owner: model-owner/infra)
   1. Create standardized artifact: model.tar.gz with config.json, tokenizer files, README.md (usage + limitations).
   2. Tag artifacts with semantic version: vMAJOR.MINOR.patch (example: v1.0.0).
   3. Upload to model-registry (internal): registry path and hash in onboarding ticket.

3. Eval-harness integration (owner: eval-infra)
   1. Add model manifest to harness: model_id, version, supported tasks, runtime constraints.
   2. Create initial prompt-set mapping (see Prompt set creation below).
   3. Schedule full evaluation run (unit + integration + performance).

4. Quantization profiling (owner: applied-ml/quantization)
   1. Generate candidate quantized builds (e.g., int8, int4 with known toolchain).
   2. Run accuracy regression vs fp16 baseline on canonical prompt sets.
   3. If delta <= configured threshold (see Quantization acceptance table), mark profile as candidate.

5. Promotion gating (owner: release-manager)
   1. All critical guardrails must pass. Any failure requires documented mitigation and a retriage.
   2. Post-promotion smoke tests on dedicated infra.

Prompt set creation and maintenance

- Naming convention: <capability>-<domain>-<version> (e.g., summarization-news-v1).
- Prompt set metadata (maintain as top-level YAML/JSON alongside examples):
  - id, name, description, owner, license, tags, provenance, creation_date, last_updated
- Minimum prompt-set quality requirements:
  - At least 250 examples for high-variance tasks (e.g., dialog, code), 1k recommended for production-critical tasks.
  - Each example has input, canonical_output(s), rubric(s) for automated scoring.
  - Diversity checks: token-length distribution, language coverage, topic coverage.

Prompt set lifecycle

1. Draft: Author creates candidates, runs local runs in harness sandbox.
2. Review: At least two reviewers from Applied ML and Product confirm task coverage and labeling fidelity.
3. Publish: Add to central prompt catalog and mark stable.
4. Versioning: Minor updates increment patch; major schema/coverage changes increment minor.

Quality guardrails (sample thresholds)

- Per-task acceptance thresholds (examples):
  | Metric                  | Acceptance (non-critical) | Acceptance (critical) | Alert level |
  |-------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------|-------------|
  | Exact-match / accuracy  | >= 70%                  | >= 85%               | P2          |
  | BLEU / ROUGE (summary)  | >= 0.35                 | >= 0.55             | P2          |
  | Toxicity (tox score)    | <= 0.08                 | <= 0.03             | P1          |
  | Hallucination rate (%)  | <= 12%                  | <= 4%               | P1          |
  | Latency (p50 prompt) ms | <= 120                  | <= 80               | P3          |

- Guardrail enforcement policy:
  - Critical failures (P1) block promotion and create an immediate regression incident in PagerDuty.
  - Non-critical (P2) require mitigation plan within 5 business days.
  - Monitoring: daily eval-harness runs for production branches; weekly rolling checks for historic models.

Quantization profiles and validation

- Profile template fields (kept as flat YAML/JSON in repo): name, bits, scheme, per_channel, symmetric, calibration_dataset_id, validation_promptsets, expected_accuracy_delta, runtime_flags, author, created_at.

- Quantization acceptance table:
  | Profile | Expected max metric delta (vs fp16) | Allowed tasks |
  |---------|-------------------------------------|---------------|
  | int8-symmetric | <= 0.5% (accuracy) or relative BLEU/ROUGE delta <= 1.0 | embeddings, classification, summarization |
  | int4-gptq      | <= 1.5% (accuracy) or relative BLEU/ROUGE delta <= 3.0 | latency-sensitive chat, token-gen |

- Validation steps:
  1. Run eval-harness on validation_promptsets with fp16 baseline and quantized build.
  2. Produce diff report (metrics + sample-level diffs) and human spot-check 50 samples for regression signatures.
  3. If borderline, add targeted prompt sets for triage.

Regression triage playbook

1. Detection
   - Automated: Nightly eval-harness runs and continuous CI checks produce regression alerts when guardrails breached.
   - Manual: User reports routed to Triage Slack channel (#eval-triage).

2. Initial Triage (15-30 min) - owner: oncall-evals
   - Verify artifact versions and hashes, confirm whether new code/model change triggered the run.
   - Reproduce locally with same harness commit and config.
   - Capture failing prompt sets and sample diffs.

3. Impact assessment (1-4 hours)
   - Classify: non-deterministic noise, metric drift, catastrophic regression, latency/perf regression.
   - Scope: how many prompt sets/tasks and which customers/flows are impacted.
   - Rollback gating: if P1 and customer-facing, prepare rollout rollback or traffic split to safe variant.

4. Root cause analysis and fix (1-72 hours)
   - Common causes: tokenizer mismatch, data preprocessing change, quantization drift, model code regression, evaluation harness bug.
   - Assign owners: infra, serving, quantization, applied-ml.
   - Create PR with fix + expanded tests and new prompt samples that capture regression.

5. Postmortem and prevention
   - For any P1 incident, publish postmortem within 5 business days. Include timeline, RCA, and preventive actions (tests, guardrail changes, CI blockers).
   - Add new prompt examples to canonical prompt set and to canary runs.

Operational tooling & CI integration

- Repositories and resources:
  - eval-harness repo (git+ssh): git@github.com:redwood/eval-harness.git
  - prompt-catalog (S3 + metadata repo): s3://redwood-eval/prompt-sets and repo at git@github.com:redwood/prompt-catalog.git
  - quant-profiles repo: git@github.com:redwood/quant-profiles.git

- CI gates:
  - Pull requests that modify model-serving code or quantization must include a CI evaluation badge: {unit, integration, performance} runs.
  - Any PR that changes prompt sets requires at least 2 approvals from Applied ML reviewers.

Sample commands and snippets

- Run a local eval harness job (example):
  ./bin/run_eval --model-path /tmp/model/v1 --prompt-set path/to/summarization-news-v1.json --output out.json --run-id local-test-20280601

- Example diff report extract (JSON lines):
  {"sample_id":"s-0001", "metric":"BLEU", "fp16": 0.412, "int4": 0.396, "delta": -0.016}

Governance and review cadence

- Quarterly: Applied ML quality review meeting to assess prompt-catalog drift, effectiveness of guardrails, and retiring obsolete prompt sets.
- Monthly: Quantization profile review to validate coverage across hardware tiers and update expected deltas.
- Continuous: Nightly runs and alerts on master branches.

Appendix: quick-reference tables

- Contact matrix:
  | Area | Primary owner | PagerDuty team |
  |------|---------------|----------------|
  | Eval harness infra | Eval Infrastructure | eval-infra-pd |
  | Prompt sets & labeling | Applied ML data | applied-ml-pd |
  | Quantization | Applied ML quant | quant-pd |

- Escalation matrix:
  1. Oncall-evals -> Team lead (Applied ML) -> Platform SRE -> CTO (for customer-impacting P1s).

Notes and references

- See related playbooks in this space for onboarding to model registry, release notes, and eval-harness runbook.
- Keep prompt examples free of customer PII and follow the data-management policy in /confluence/policies-and-process/data-management.
